 Follow FDA Announces Nationwide Recall on Toothpaste and Mouthwash Due to Potential Health Risks
 Here’s what to know.
 Natalie Onkst Updated Fri, November 13, 2026 at 7:23 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Credit: Design elements: Getty Images. EatingWell design. Key Takeaways
 ORL Labs is recalling over 51,000 oral care products due to contamination with hormones.
 Affected toothpaste and mouthwash products were sold nationwide and should be discarded or returned.
 The recall is classified as Class II, meaning it may cause temporary health effects if used.
 ORL Labs announced an ongoing nationwide recall for various Organic Oral care products, according to the Food and Drug Administration. This is due to cross-contamination with the presence of progesterone, estradiol or dehydroepiandrosterone found within the items.
 This specific recall affects approximately 51,762 units of Organic Oral Care toothpaste brands and mouth wash such as Organic Oral Care Bubblegum Kids natural toothpaste, Organic Oral Care Cinnamint toothpaste and Organic Oral Care Bubblegum Kids mouthwash. The affected products were sold nationwide and can be identified by their specific lot codes and expiration dates below.

 There are no reported illnesses from using the recalled products, but if you have any of the above-listed toothpaste tubes or mouthwashes, discard them immediately or return them to your local retailer for a potential refund.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This recall has been classified as Class II, meaning it may cause "temporary" health consequences. For questions about this recall, contact the FDA at 1-888-INFO-FDA (1-888-463-6332).
